items.title: Supreme Court bans construction activities within 100 meters of Rajasthan's Jojari River
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday banned all construction and development activities within 100 metres from the edge of Rajasthan's Jojari River till the conclusion of scientific determination and demarcation of the high flood line and ecological buffer zones [ In Re: 2 Million Lives At Risk, Contamination In Jojari River, Rajasthan ]. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta passed the order in a suo motu case concerning industrial pollution of rivers in Rajasthan, including the Jojari River. " We are of the considered view that it is necessary to put in place an interim, definite and measurable area of protection so as to adequately safeguard the riverine ecosystem during the pendency of the scientific exercise for the determination and demarcation of the high flood line and the requisite ecological buffer zones. Hence, we hereby direct that no construction or development activity of any nature whatsoever shall be permitted within a distance of 100 meters from the edge of the river in accordance with the aforesaid guidelines," the Court ordered. items.summary: “ It is madness to risk what you have and need for what you don't need. ” Warren Buffett, the Oracle of Omaha, has long cautioned against investment vehicles that offer a usually win, occasionally die payoff, likening excessive risk-taking to a game of Russian Roulette: the odds may favour you most of the time, but any one bad outcome can be catastrophic. items.title: ‘The later it gets, the crazier the shows become’: US ambassador Sergio Gor on the chaos of Indian TV news
items.summary: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor appears to have discovered a guilty pleasure familiar to many an NRI uncle: watching Indian television news for entertainment. Speaking on a range of issues at the Economic Times World Leaders Forum in New Delhi, Gor offered what may be the most diplomatic review yet of Indian prime-time TV – marvelling at the sheer number of people who can shout simultaneously while technically being on the same programme. “I love getting back home and watching Indian TV news shows. The later it gets, the crazier the shows become. At 6 pm you have 8 people arguing on the show. At 10 pm, there are 12 people who are all speaking at the same time. You can’t hear a single one of them…it’s unbelievable that no one gets interrupted,” he said. For context: American cable news is no stranger to volume, hostility, or the occasional shouting match. But even hardened veterans of that particular arena, it seems, regard the 10-person, simultaneous-speech format of Indian prime-time as a genre of its own. A Bench of Justice Satish Chandra Sharma and Justice NK Singh held that the NGT had failed to establish a causal link between the festival and the alleged environmental degradation. The Court directed the Delhi Development Authority (DDA) to refund the ₹5 crore deposited by the organisation as environmental compensation. The order was passed on an appeal filed by Vyakti Vikas Kendra India (VVKI), the Indian organisation associated with the Art of Living Foundation, founded by spiritual leader Sri Sri Ravi Shankar. The Art of Living Foundation is the broader international organisation, while VVKI is a separate Indian entity associated with it. The Court found that there was sufficient material to show that the event site was already in a poor condition before it was handed over to VVKI.
